title: Ackee Rundown
subtitle: Ackee simmered in coconut milk with scotch bonnet and spring onion
excerpt: Tinned ackee folded into a spiced coconut milk sauce with scotch bonnet and thyme. Quick to make and deeply savoury. Eat with boiled dumplings or rice.
sourceNotes: Jamaican rundown tradition. The name comes from running down the coconut milk into a thick sauce. Ackee version is a vegetarian take on the classic salt fish and ackee combination.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made a day ahead and refrigerated. Fold in the ackee gently when reheating to avoid breaking the pieces.

content.text: Rundown is all about reducing the coconut milk until it thickens into a rich sauce. Ackee breaks apart easily, so add it right at the end. Handle it gently or the pieces will turn to mush.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the garlic, scotch bonnet, and thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes until it starts to break down. Season with the allspice, black pepper, and a good pinch of salt.
Pour in the coconut milk. Bring to a steady simmer and cook uncovered for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce reduces by about a third and thickens.
Add the spring onion and stir through. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Gently lower the drained ackee into the sauce. Do not stir. Shake the pan gently to coat the pieces. Heat through for 3 minutes without disturbing.
Serve immediately with rice or boiled dumplings.

items.cause: It was stirred too vigorously or added too early.
items.fix: Add the ackee at the very end, after all the sauce is ready, and fold in gently with a spoon rather than stirring.

items.cause: It was not reduced for long enough before adding the ackee.
items.fix: Simmer the coconut milk sauce on its own until it noticeably thickens before adding any other ingredients.

items.cause: Scotch bonnet heat varies enormously between chillies.
items.fix: Use only a small piece to start and taste the sauce before adding the ackee. Remove the scotch bonnet whole rather than dicing if you want mild heat.
